bookingUrls.label: Super Corporate Jet / Boeing Business Jet

notes: Owner confirmed as Karan Gogna. Resolves {{custom_values.business_owner}}, which appears in the About page copy; the rest of the site keeps company-front framing.

The phone number is a 714 area code (Orange County, CA) for a business operating out of NJ/NY/PA airports. Mobile numbers travel, so this is not necessarily wrong — but a local 201/862/973 number reads as more credible to a Teterboro flight department, and area code is one of the few local-SEO signals a service business has. Worth raising with the client.

The contact email is a personal Gmail address, and it will render publicly on Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, and Request a Quote as the business contact. jetspa.co already exists as a domain; a karan@jetspa.co style address would cost nothing and match the credential-heavy positioning the copy leans on.
websiteUrl: the domain jetspa.co is stated in the client's Privacy Policy as 'http://jetspa.co'. Recorded here as https — confirm the canonical scheme and whether www redirects.

theme: 'chrome' + #1f6f8b is a proposal, not an observation. Preset choice and accent are the only design decisions in this file; confirm with the client before the first build. Contrast is validated at build time.

legal.source is 'client': JetSpa supplied its own Privacy Policy and Terms of Service with aviation-specific insurance, warranty, and AOG liability clauses. That text has NOT been through Detailer Systems' legal review.
areas are airports, not cities, so `state` is deliberately null on all four — this drives both the '{name}, {ST}' label suppression and Place (not City) in LocalBusiness JSON-LD.
isHeadquarters is false on all four airports: the export never states which field the business is based out of. Set one if KTEB (or another) is the home base.

9 service pages, of which 3 are aircraft-class segment pages (corporate jet / turboprop / piston) that sell a customer segment rather than a distinct service. They share the services collection and route.
Booking is organised by aircraft class, not vehicle type — 6 calendars, all still to be built in GHL.
Pricing rule from the client: no dollar amounts, tiers, or starting prices on any live page. Pricing is disclosed by phone, quote form, or the booking calendar.

8 service pages carry a [BEFORE/AFTER IMAGE SECTION] placeholder in the export; assets.beforeAfter is empty until real photography exists. Generated aircraft imagery is a poor fit for this audience — wrong airframes and garbled registrations are obvious to owners and flight departments.

Trust signals repeated site-wide and treated as facts: ADA (Aircraft Detailing Association) certification, OEM-approved chemistry, $200K general liability + $1.5M hangar liability insurance, badge access at all four airports. Verify each before publishing; none is verifiable from the export.
Morristown's ICAO is KMMU (the onboarding call said 'MMA', which is wrong).

PLACEHOLDERS ARE IN USE, by decision: site.config.ts carries stand-in values for the facts still null here, so the site can be built and reviewed before onboarding completes. This file stays the honest record — a field that is null here has not been supplied, whatever site.config.ts says. Every placeholder contains the string 'PLACEHOLDER', is listed on every build by src/lib/site-config.ts, and fails the build under DS_STRICT=1. Assets are generated stand-ins from `pnpm run placeholders jetspa`, not photography.

Instagram is the only social account; Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and the Google review link are deliberately skipped. SocialLinks and the FAQs CTA are config-driven and handle their absence on their own, but the EXPORT COPY does not: Request a Quote and Booking Confirmed name all four platforms inline, and FAQs links a review button. Those sentences must be rewritten to Instagram-only while authoring the payload — leaving the tokens in place fails the build.
